_comment: Curated CVE intelligence for the demo's 'patch by risk' view. The DEFAULT (offline, stage-reliable) source for autopackager/services/cve_intel.py. Every entry is a REAL public CVE with its REAL NVD CVSS v3.1 base score and the upstream version that fixes it ('fixed_in'). A CVE only counts against a deployed app when fixed_in is NEWER than what's deployed, so a current app shows green and an outdated one lights up. To stage the demo: deploy a deliberately-old build (see fixed_in) and it goes red; upgrade clears it. Update against https://nvd.nist.gov as scores/fixes change. Keyed by product; resolved via cpe (catalog 'cpe' field) or any 'aliases' name slug.

cves.summary: Integer overflow while parsing a crafted MMS stream leads to a heap-based buffer overflow — a malicious stream can crash VLC or run code with the user's privileges.
Integer underflow in the Zstandard (Zstd) decompression path allows remote code execution via a crafted archive opened in 7-Zip.
Mark-of-the-Web bypass: files extracted from a crafted nested archive do not inherit MotW, letting attacker content execute without the SmartScreen warning (exploited in the wild).
Notepad++ installer privilege escalation via an uncontrolled executable search path — run from a user-writable folder it loads a planted system binary, giving a local user SYSTEM.

tarfile extraction-filter bypass: a crafted tar archive can modify file metadata and escape the destination directory despite the 'data' filter, an RCE-class flaw. (Fixed across the 3.9.23 / 3.10.18 / 3.11.13 / 3.12.3 branches.)
tarfile denial of service: a tar archive with a negative header offset drives the extraction routine into an infinite loop / deadlock.
crypto/x509: setting ExtKeyUsageAny in VerifyOptions.KeyUsages unintentionally disables policy validation, weakening certificate-chain verification for chains carrying policy constraints.
